TestLimits::test_accepted_large_request.description: Single node, --smp 2, --memory 2G, --commitlog-total-space-in-mb 1024, run over SSL and non-SSL CQL. Inserts a ~30MB text value (bigger than half a commitlog segment, i.e. oversized/fragmented commitlog entry), reads it back from a new session and asserts equality, then overwrites with a 6MB value and reads it back. Guards scylladb/scylladb#19472 (commitlog: handle oversized entries) end-to-end through CQL, incl. large TLS frames.

origin.summary: Added as a 'semi-copy' of test_request_too_large when commitlog started accepting oversized mutations (scylladb#19472); fixes scylla-dtest#4953.

TestLimits::test_max_columns_and_query_p.description: Single node (4G, long request/raft timeouts). Creates tables with 2^n-1 columns for n=1..16 (up to 65535 int columns), inserts one row with all columns, drops the table; at 131071 columns expects CREATE TABLE to fail with raft 'Command size N is greater than the configured limit M'. Guards schema changes with very wide tables and the group0 max command size limit (max_command_size = schema commitlog max_record_size/2).

TestLimits::test_request_too_large.description: Single node --smp 2 (default 512MB/shard), commitlog total 60MB / segment 6MB, SSL and non-SSL. Inserts a ~30MB string and expects NoHostAvailable, WriteFailure or InvalidRequest; then from a new session asserts the row is absent, and that a 6MB insert succeeds and reads back. Originally (2022) guarded scylla fa29b79c2 'close connection on too large request' (memory-based shedding); since 752dce7bb4 intended to hit commitlog 'Mutation ... too large for potentially available disk space'.

origin.summary: Test that too-large CQL request (>10% shard memory) gets connection closed, SSL and non-SSL (scylla commit fa29b79c2).

TestLimits::test_request_too_large.reason: Assertion is weak: accepts any of NoHostAvailable/WriteFailure/InvalidRequest, so it can't tell which path rejected the request. With default 512MB/shard the shed limit is ~48MB (msg in ef7a42edb9) vs ~62MB estimate for the 30MB frame, so CQL shedding (covered by cqlpy test_shed_too_large_request) likely always fires first and the 60MB-commitlog path is never reached. Note: SSL helper uses deprecated PROTOCOL_TLSv1_2 workaround for CLOSED python-driver#261.

TestMaxCQLConnections::test_max_cql_conn.description: Single node --smp 1 with --max-networking-io-control-blocks 10500; spawns 10 subprocesses (scripts/create_dummy_cql_connections.py) each opening 1050 driver sessions, asserts all 10500 created and scylla_transport_cql_connections{shard=0} >= created, closes them, repeats once. Regression for 2021 crash at >10000 connections per shard (scylladb PR #9052 / commit 2cfc517874 'adjust number of networking iocbs').

origin.summary: Test that many CQL connections (5x3000) can be opened and re-opened after close, verifying scylla PR #9052.

TestMaxCQLConnections::test_max_cql_conn.reason: No scylla test opens >10k CQL connections, but checks are weak. Bug: scylla_transport_cql_connections is a cumulative counter (transport/server.cc:350 make_counter('cql-connections', _stats.connects)), not the current_connections gauge, so the second assert after closing is trivially true and connection release isn't actually verified. Note: `except ValueError` (limits_test.py:279) can't catch the AttributeError from a failed regex match, so the diagnostic message is dead. Note: passes --max-networking-io-control-blocks 10500, lowering scylla's default 50000 (main.cc:761), so default config isn't tested; slow (~125s).
